outcome: Admission to neonatal intensive care unit
cohort: 415 women who underwent gastric bypass surgery between 1996 and 2011 and subsequently gave birth in Denmark
finding: Women who had undergone gastric bypass surgery had a lower risk of preeclampsia, emergency cesarean section, and perinatal asphyxia compared with adipose women without surgery, but a higher risk of hypertension, gestational diabetes, and acute abdominal pain during pregnancy compared with normal weight controls, and their children had a lower birthweight and higher incidence of admittance to neonatal intensive care compared with newborn of normal weight mothers.
mod_finding: Women who underwent gastric bypass had a lower incidence of emergency cesarean sections compared to adipose women without surgery.
